scope: Source evidence for the two bench-staged angular-reflection reconstructions. Geometry is built for review; exact dimensions, installed configuration, optical alignment and manipulation remain unqualified.

sources.inspected: Supplementary Note 3, printed page 14: text rechecked. Nicolet 6700, SpectraTech variable-angle accessory and Harrick 12-degree specular accessory are named. Exact accessory SKUs, mounts and stage variants are not supplied.

Both pages rendered and visually inspected: VR1-HRS horizontal stage, VR1-VWA-12 absolute-reflection stage and separate VRX optical bases. Horizontal samples face down; the HRS stage alone is not a complete accessory.
Official front three-quarter image: open bracket, apertured horizontal top, sloped reflector assembly and a separate circular mask. No measured outer or mating dimensions.
Manufacturer product description and image link. Plug-in horizontal 12-degree stage with interchangeable 3, 6 and 13 mm aperture masks.

Zero-based pages 141-143 / printed 125-127 rendered and visually inspected. Three optical-base diagrams distinguish the central four-mirror FTIR model from the outer UV-Vis models. Legacy base code is VR1-XXX. Zero-based page 73 code-chart text inspected; Avatar/Nexus are listed but Nicolet 6700 is not.
sources.limits: No outer/mount dimensions or established 6700 adapter. The text extractor reads the Avatar/Nexus code as N18; do not use an unverified OCR code for part selection.

candidate_decisions.candidate: VR1-HRS horizontal stage plus a separately reconstructed FTIR optical base
candidate_decisions.basis: Authored demo choice among documented 12-degree arrangements. The face-down horizontal stage supports a concrete loading interface without claiming the paper's unreported variant.
do_not_substitute: VR1-VWA-12 double-reflection frame relabeled as HRS
An HRS stage without its required optical base
unresolved: Exact base variant and 6700 mating hardware
candidate_decisions.dimensional_hypotheses: Base 190 x 220 x 10 mm; HRS stage 60 x 54 x 63 mm; masks OD20 mm. Only 3/6/13 mm mask apertures come from the manufacturer. Outer scale, mirror curvature, optical height, local supports, sockets and fasteners are inferred.
candidate_decisions.interpretation: The circular dark region in the sloped mirror photograph is treated as a reflection of the upper aperture, not a through-hole; the line drawing depicts a solid mirror.

candidate_decisions.basis: The depicted 500 geometry and right-to-left path match the direction shown in the Nicolet 6700 manual. This is a reconstruction candidate, not proof of historical model or mounting compatibility.
rejected_shortcuts: Selecting 501 solely because its catalogue row lists Nicolet Impact
Treating a photograph of model 500 as exact model 501 CAD
Inventing a fifth independent M4 mirror plus a separate specimen; the rejected GLB remains in angular_topology_rejected.json
unresolved: Manufacturer linkage, angle-dependent finite-aperture coverage and focus
candidate_decisions.dimensional_hypotheses: The 180 x 100 x 8 mm base and 170 x 6 x 175 mm backplate are unchanged hypotheses. Four independent mirrors and a removable M4 reference now replace the rejected six-surface topology. The selected common M3/M4 carrier has a 165 mm pivot height and 15 mm left offset beside the source housing, 26 mm sample lever and a perpendicular pair of optical planes; exact linkage and pivot are not established by the schematic. The local optical plane and inferred port centre move from Y-25 to Y-20 mm to clear the housing while retaining mirror widths and the external envelope. A coherent initial 20-degree center ray is checked, but finite-aperture misses over the range remain explicit. Frame, spring retainers, mounts, forces and optical calibration are unqualified.
